tags.description:en:1: The toponym derives etymologically by composition of "rondine" (swallow) and "nera" (black), and literally translates into English as "Blackswallow", however the birds which every spring-summer populate the skies of Rondinera pertain to the species
tags.description:en:2: of common swifts (Apus apus), not to that of swallows (Hirundo rustica);
tags.description:en:3: another species common in the summer period is that of the Italian sparrow (Passer italiae).
